newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse CEO says sees TV consolidations.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse CEO says sees TV consolidations.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Michael Jordan said Monday he expects the rising costs of producing television to lead to consolidations in the industry.

Speaking at the National Association of Broadcasters convention, Jordan said the total costs of television are rising at between 10 and 15 percent a year while revenue increases are not matching that pace.
Jordan said the Telecommunications Act of 1996, which led to a spate of acquisitions in the radio industry, is an indication of the possibilities of consolidation.
Media companies, such as Westinghouse's CBS Network, show the possibilities of the cross-marketing of television and radio, he said.
For the first time, radio really has an opportunity "to take on newspapers," he said.

Jordan also said it's time to change the way advertising prices are measured, which he said is based on an antiquated model of a three-channel market. He said the current system of measuring does not reflect the growing number of channels.
Instead, Jordan said, the industry should look at demographic statistics other than age, which do not always reflect a viewer's buying power.
While 80 percent of consumer spending is done by people 35 years and older, the bulk of advertising is geared to appeal to a younger audience.
